questions.stem: A mixture of \(100\) litres contains milk and water in the ratio \(3:2\). How many litres of water must be added to make the ratio \(1:1\)?
questions.keySolution:
Initial mixture = \(100\) litres with ratio \(3:2\)
Milk = \(\frac{3}{5} \times 100 = 60\) litres
Water = \(\frac{2}{5} \times 100 = 40\) litres
For ratio \(1:1\), milk = water = \(60\) litres
Water to be added = \(60 - 40 = 20\) litres

questions.stem: In a \(45\) litre mixture of milk and water, milk is \(60\%\). How many litres of water should be added to make milk \(50\%\) of the mixture?
questions.keySolution:
Initial mixture = \(45\) litres
Milk = \(60\%\) of \(45 = 27\) litres
Let \(x\) litres of water be added
\(\frac{27}{45 + x} = \frac{50}{100}\)
\(54 = 45 + x\)
\(x = 9\) litres

\(30 = 15 + 3x\)

questions.stem: A container has \(90\) litres of pure milk. If \(30\) litres of water is added, what is the ratio of milk to water?
